mainTopic: The reasons behind the י״ח דברים, the rabbinic decrees that make תרומה פסול: eating and drinking impure items, מים שאובים, a ספר, and hands.
overview: This amud explains the reasons behind the י״ח דברים, the rabbinic decrees that make תרומה פסול. First the גמרא asks why the list says these items only 'disqualify' תרומה. רבה בר בר חנה answers that the list follows רבי יהושע, who holds that eating impure food makes a person only a שני. Next the גמרא explains the decrees on eating impure food and drinking impure liquids: both stop a person from ruining תרומה inside his own mouth. Both are listed because one case is common and the other is rare. The decree on מים שאובים was made because rinsing with drawn water after טבילה had become a fixed habit. אביי and רבא argue about what danger that habit caused. A pure person hit by drawn water was included so that the first decree would hold. A ספר was made able to disqualify תרומה so that people would stop storing תרומה beside it. Hands were included because they are always busy, and hands that touched a ספר were included because of רבי יוחנן's warning against holding a bare ספר תורה. At the end, the גמרא begins asking which hand-decree came first, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why do these items only disqualify and not render impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its question: the list says these items make תרומה פסול, so does that mean they do not make it טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: ...[they disqualify the תרומה, but] they do not make it impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question from the previous page about the list of rabbinic decrees. The list says these impurities only make תרומה פסול, and the גמרא asks why it does not say they make it טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that is פסול is ruined but cannot pass impurity on to anything else. Something that is טמא can spread impurity further. Since a person who ate a ראשון might be expected to become a ראשון himself, the גמרא wonders why the list treats him so lightly.

keyTerms.meaning: they render impure, meaning the item becomes able to pass impurity on further
they disqualify, meaning the item is ruined but does not spread impurity
the portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be eaten in purity

steps.confusionAlert: פסול and טמא are not the same thing here. פסול means 'ruined, but it stops there.' טמא means 'impure, and it can make other things impure too.'

phrases.english: they do not render [it] impure?
phrases.notes: This finishes a question that started on the previous page, about the decrees that 'disqualify תרומה'.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מְטַמּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous page about the list of eighteen decrees.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the list says these items only disqualify תרומה instead of making it fully impure.

steps.title: The list follows רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה answers that the list follows the view of רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: This follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה answers the question by saying the list follows the opinion of רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהושע, a person who eats impure food becomes at most a שני. A שני that touches תרומה only makes it פסול, not טמא. So the wording 'disqualify' fits his view exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'it is' — this teaching follows that opinion

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
It is [the view of] Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the teaching to a specific תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating impure food should make a person as impure as the food, so the list should say 'render impure.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The list follows רבי יהושע, under whom the eater is only a שני, so he only disqualifies.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the eater takes on the same level as the food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. In it, רבי אליעזר says a person who eats impure food becomes the same level as the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר says: One who eats a ראשון food becomes a ראשון. One who eats a שני food becomes a שני. One who eats a שלישי food becomes a שלישי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the disagreement, starting with רבי אליעזר's view. He holds the eater becomes the same level as the food he ate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי אליעזר, someone who ate a ראשון is himself a ראשון. A ראשון makes תרומה fully טמא, not just פסול. That is why the list cannot follow him.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who eats first-degree food is first-degree.
And one who eats second-degree food is second-degree.
[One who eats] third-degree food is third-degree.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins quoting the משנה that backs up רבה בר בר חנה's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a view under which the eater of impure food is less impure than the food.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה in טהרות containing the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the eater is at most a second-degree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says that eating a ראשון or a שני makes one a שני. Eating a שלישי makes one a שני for קודש but not for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: One who eats a ראשון food or a שני food becomes a שני. One who eats a שלישי food becomes a שני regarding קודש, but not a שני regarding תרומה. This case of a שלישי can only happen with חולין that were prepared with the purity standards of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with רבי יהושע's view. This is the view the list of decrees follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, even eating a ראשון only makes a person a שני. A שני only makes תרומה פסול, which explains the wording of the list. The last line explains that a שלישי food can only exist in חולין that were deliberately kept to the purity level of תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: sacrificial or holy items, which have the strictest purity rules
prepared according to the purity standards of תרומה

steps.whatToRemember: The list of decrees says 'disqualify' because it follows רבי יהושע. In his view, eating impure food makes a person only a שני, and a שני ruins תרומה without making it able to spread impurity.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹכֵל אוֹכֶל רִאשׁוֹן וְאוֹכֶל שֵׁנִי — שֵׁנִי.
phrases.english: One who eats first-degree food or second-degree food is second-degree.
[One who eats] third-degree [food] is second-degree for consecrated items,
but not second-degree for teruma,
[this is] with non-sacred food prepared with the purity of teruma.
phrases.notes: Explains how a person could even come to eat third-degree food.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה begun in step 3 and supplies the view the answer relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That the eater of a ראשון is only a שני, so he only disqualifies תרומה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's statement in the משנה.

steps.title: Why did the Rabbis decree impurity on one who eats impure food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the decree making someone who ate impure food impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who eats a ראשון food or a שני food — what is the reason the רבנן decreed impurity on him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question: why did the רבנן make this decree in the first place? This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, eating impure food does not make a person impure. So the גמרא wants to know what problem the רבנן were trying to prevent.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹכֵל אוֹכֶל רִאשׁוֹן וְאוֹכֵל אוֹכֶל שֵׁנִי —
phrases.english: One who eats first-degree food and one who eats second-degree food —

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה?
phrases.english: what is the reason the Rabbis decreed impurity upon him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the wording of the decree to the reason behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the decree on one who eats impure food.

steps.title: So he won't ruin תרומה liquids in his mouth
steps.stepSummary: The decree prevents someone who just ate impure food from drinking תרומה liquids, which would touch the impure food in his mouth and become ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because sometimes a person eats impure food, then takes תרומה liquids and puts them into his mouth, and ruins them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the decree. Leftover impure food in the mouth would touch the תרומה drink and ruin it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pieces of impure food stay in the mouth after eating. When the person drinks תרומה liquid, it touches that food and becomes פסול. To prevent this, the רבנן made the eater himself impure, so he stays away from תרומה entirely.

phrases.english: Because sometimes he eats impure foods,
and takes liquids of teruma,
and casts [them] into his mouth and disqualifies them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּזִימְנִין דְּאָכֵיל אוֹכָלִין טְמֵאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree is a safeguard so the eater won't ruin תרומה liquids in his mouth.

steps.title: Why did the Rabbis decree impurity on one who drinks impure liquids?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the decree on someone who drank impure liquids.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who drinks impure liquids — what is the reason the רבנן decreed impurity on him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same question about the next decree on the list. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the previous case: drinking impure liquids instead of eating impure food.

phrases.english: One who drinks impure liquids —

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה?
phrases.english: what is the reason the Rabbis decreed impurity upon him?

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹתֶה מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question about the next decree.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the decree on one who drinks impure liquids.

steps.title: So he won't ruin תרומה food in his mouth
steps.stepSummary: The decree prevents someone who just drank impure liquid from putting תרומה food in his mouth, where the impure liquid would ruin it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because sometimes a person drinks impure liquids, then takes תרומה foods, puts them into his mouth, and ruins them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of reason, with the roles reversed: impure liquid in the mouth would ruin תרומה food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure liquid left in the mouth would touch the תרומה food and make it פסול. So the רבנן decreed that the drinker himself is impure and must stay away from תרומה.

phrases.english: Because sometimes he drinks impure liquids,
and takes foods of teruma
and casts [them] into his mouth and disqualifies them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּזִימְנִין דְּשָׁתֵי מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree is a safeguard so the drinker won't ruin תרומה food in his mouth.

steps.title: Aren't these two decrees really the same?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: both decrees have the same reason, so why are they listed as two separate decrees?
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this the same as that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list. If both decrees have the same reason, why count them as two separate decrees?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both decrees work the same way: impure stuff in the mouth ruins תרומה. If one decree covered both cases, the list would seem to be counting the same thing twice.

keyTerms.meaning: 'this is the same as that' — a challenge that two things are identical

phrases.english: Isn't this the same as that?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ הָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for both decrees after hearing their identical reasons.
steps.kashyaTarget: Listing eating and drinking impure items as two separate decrees.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Same reason means one decree, so the list should not count it twice.

steps.title: One case is common, the other is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: drinking after eating is common, but eating while impure liquid is still in the mouth is not. Without the second decree, we might think the רבנן did not decree for the uncommon case.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: this case is common, and that case is not common. So it teaches us that both were decreed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why both decrees are needed. One case is common, and we might have thought the רבנן would skip the uncommon one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People often drink while or after eating, so ruining תרומה liquid is a real risk. Putting food in the mouth while it is still wet with liquid is rare. Listing the second decree separately teaches that the רבנן decreed even for the rare case.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

phrases.english: Lest you say:
this is common, and that is not common —
it teaches us [otherwise].

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא הָא שְׁכִיחִי וְהָא לָא שְׁכִיחִי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the second case adds something new (common vs. uncommon)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן only decreed for the common case of eating impure food.
steps.terutzMaskana: They decreed even for the uncommon case of drinking impure liquids, so both are listed.
steps.whatToRemember: The decrees on eating impure food and drinking impure liquids have the same reason: protecting תרומה from being ruined in the mouth. Both are listed to teach that the רבנן decreed even in the less common case.

steps.title: Why the decree on one who enters drawn water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן made someone impure when his head and most of his body enter מים שאובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one whose head and most of his body enter drawn water — what is the reason the רבנן decreed impurity on him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another decree on the list and asks for its reason. This sets up רב אסי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מים שאובים is water that was drawn or carried in a vessel. It seems strange that ordinary water would make someone impure, so the גמרא wants the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: his head and the majority of his body
drawn water — water carried or drawn using a vessel

phrases.english: And one whose head and most [of his body] enter drawn water —

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה?
phrases.english: what is the reason the Rabbis decreed impurity upon him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַבָּא רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ בְּמַיִם שְׁאוּבִין מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next decree in the list of eighteen.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the decree on one who enters מים שאובים.

steps.title: Rinsing with drawn water after immersion became a fixed practice
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי in the name of רב אסי explains: people immersed in foul cave water and then rinsed with drawn water. When this became a fixed practice, the רבנן decreed that drawn water makes a person impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said in the name of רב אסי: At first, people would immerse in cave water that was gathered, still, and foul. Afterward they would pour drawn water on themselves. Once they started treating this as a fixed practice, the רבנן decreed impurity on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי, quoting רב אסי, tells the history behind the decree. Rinsing with drawn water after immersion had become a routine part of the process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cave water was valid for טבילה, but it smelled bad, so people rinsed off with drawn water. Once this became routine, people might come to think the drawn water was what made them pure. The רבנן decreed that drawn water on the head and most of the body makes one impure, which put an end to the practice.
steps.confusionAlert: The cave water itself was a valid מקוה; the טבילה worked. The decree is about the drawn water poured on afterward, not about the immersion being invalid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a typical reason for a rabbinic decree: the רבנן step in when a harmless habit becomes fixed and could mislead people about what really makes a person pure.
steps.whatToRemember: The decree on מים שאובים was made because rinsing with drawn water after טבילה had become a fixed habit. The רבנן wanted to stop people from treating drawn water as part of becoming pure.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Beivai said that Rav Asi said:
For originally they would immerse
in cave water that was collected and foul,
and they would pour drawn water upon themselves.
They began and made it a fixed practice —
[so] they decreed impurity upon them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר רַב אַסִּי שֶׁבַּתְּחִלָּה הָיוּ טוֹבְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rinsing with drawn water after immersing in foul cave water had become a fixed practice, so the רבנן decreed drawn water makes one impure to stop it.

steps.title: What does 'fixed practice' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what was meant by saying the rinsing with drawn water became קבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'fixed'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word קבע from רב ביבי's explanation. This sets up the next move, where אביי and רבא define it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rinsing off after טבילה is harmless in itself. So the גמרא needs to know what about the 'fixed practice' made it dangerous enough to need a decree.

phrases.english: What is 'fixed'?
phrases.notes: Refers back to רב ביבי's words in step 12.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a term used in the previous answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly became 'fixed' that bothered the רבנן?

steps.title: אביי: people thought both waters together purify
steps.stepSummary: אביי says people began to think that the cave water alone does not purify, only the cave water and the drawn water together.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: people would say, 'It is not this water alone that purifies. Both this and that purify together.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers: the 'fixed practice' was a mistaken belief that both kinds of water together make a person pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the danger is a wrong idea. People were treating the drawn water as part of the purification.

phrases.english: Abaye said: that they would say:
'Not these (cave waters alone) purify,'
'rather these and those together purify.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what קבע means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mistaken belief that cave water and drawn water purify together.

steps.title: רבא: what harm is there if they still immerse?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי: even with that belief, people still immerse in the proper water, so nothing goes wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: What difference does it make? They are still immersing in those (proper) waters!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's explanation. He says that belief causes no real harm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people still do a proper טבילה in the cave water, then they become pure, even if they misunderstand why. So אביי's version gives no real reason for a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: what practical difference does it make

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
What difference does it make,
aren't they immersing in those (valid waters)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: מַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wrong belief causes no harm if the valid טבילה still happens, so it cannot justify a decree.

steps.title: רבא: people thought only the drawn water purifies
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the danger was that people would think the drawn water is what purifies, not the cave water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: people would say, 'It is not these (cave waters) that purify. Rather, those (drawn waters) purify.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own explanation of קבע. People would come to think only the drawn water makes you pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the harm is real. People might skip the proper טבילה and use only drawn water, which does not purify. That is why the רבנן decreed that drawn water makes a person impure.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's version wins: the decree on מים שאובים stops people from thinking drawn water purifies, which would lead them to skip real טבילה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: that they would say:
'Not these (cave waters) purify,'
'rather those (drawn waters) purify.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fear was that people would think only drawn water purifies.

steps.title: Why decree on a pure person hit by drawn water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן made impure a pure person who had three לוגין of drawn water fall on his head and most of his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a pure person on whose head and most of his body three לוגין of drawn water fell: what is the reason the רבנן decreed impurity on him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the list of decrees. It asks why a person who was already pure becomes impure from drawn water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reason was about people who had just immersed. This person did not immerse at all, so that reason does not seem to apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: a person who is already ritually pure
his head and most of his body

phrases.english: And a pure person upon whose head and most of his body fell
three log of drawn water —

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה?
phrases.english: what is the reason the Rabbis decreed impurity on him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next decree on the list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for decreeing impurity on someone who never immersed.

steps.title: Without this decree, the first one would not hold
steps.stepSummary: The second decree is needed to protect the first. Otherwise people would not keep the first decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if not for this decree, that one would not stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this decree supports the earlier one about drawn water after טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only someone who just immersed became impure from drawn water, people would mix up the cases and treat the first decree lightly. Making every pure person impure from drawn water keeps the rule simple and firm.

phrases.english: For if not for this (decree),
that (first decree) would not stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא הָא, לָא קָיְימָא הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the pure person.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a protective decree that makes the first decree hold up.

steps.title: Why decree impurity on a ספר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן decreed that a ספר makes things impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ספר: what is the reason the רבנן decreed impurity on it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the list and asks the reason for the decree on a ספר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems strange that something as holy as a ספר תורה would be declared impure. So the reason needs to be explained.

phrases.english: And a scroll — what is the reason
the Rabbis decreed impurity on it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסֵפֶר — מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next decree on the list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a holy ספר would be given impurity.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: תרומה stored by the ספר attracted damage
steps.stepSummary: People stored תרומה food next to the ספר תורה, saying both are holy. This led to damage, so the רבנן decreed impurity to keep them apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: at first they would hide תרומה food next to the ספר תורה, and say, 'This is holy and that is holy.' Once the רבנן saw it was leading to damage, they decreed impurity on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא explains the decree on a ספר. It was made to stop people from keeping תרומה next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food attracted mice, which also chewed the ספר. By declaring that the ספר makes תרומה פסול, the רבנן made sure no one would store תרומה near it again. The decree protects the ספר; it does not lower its holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: the holy portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The decree is not because the ספר is impure in a real sense. It was made to protect the ספר from damage.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
For at first they would store teruma foods
next to a Torah scroll,
and they said: 'This is holy and that is holy.'
Once they saw that it was coming to damage,
phrases.notes: Mice drawn to the food would chew the scroll.

phrases.english: the Rabbis decreed impurity on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: שֶׁבִּתְחִלָּה הָיוּ מַצְנִיעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the ספר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To stop people from storing תרומה near the ספר, which led to damage.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rabbinic decree of טומאה can be a protective tool, not a statement that the object is lowly.

steps.title: Hands are impure because they are always busy
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן decreed impurity on hands because hands touch things without a person paying attention.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the hands: because hands are busy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the next item on the list, the decree on hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People touch all kinds of dirty or impure things without noticing. So the רבנן made hands פסול for תרומה unless they are washed.

phrases.english: And the hands — because hands are busy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיָּדַיִם — מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַיָּדַיִם עַסְקָנִיּוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next decree on the list, giving the question and the reason together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hands are made impure because they touch things without attention.

steps.title: Hands that touch a ספר also disqualify תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that hands that touched a ספר also make תרומה פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: even hands that come from touching a ספר disqualify תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that adds a second decree about hands. This sets up the next step, which explains the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a separate source of hand impurity. It does not come from the hands being busy. It comes from touching a ספר directly.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא, אַף יָדַיִם הַבָּאוֹת מֵחֲמַת סֵפֶר
phrases.english: It was taught: even hands that come (to impurity) because of a scroll
disqualify the teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא, אַף יָדַיִם הַבָּאוֹת מֵחֲמַת סֵפֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further case of hand impurity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hands that touched a ספר disqualify תרומה.

steps.title: Reason: רבי פרנך on holding a bare ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: The decree comes from רבי פרנך's teaching in the name of רבי יוחנן: one who holds a ספר תורה bare will be buried bare.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is because of רבי פרנך, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: one who holds a ספר תורה bare is buried bare.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason for the decree on hands that touch a ספר. The רבנן wanted people to stop touching an uncovered ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching a bare ספר תורה is disrespectful, and רבי יוחנן warns of a harsh punishment for it. The decree makes such hands פסול for תרומה, which discourages people from touching the ספר directly.
steps.confusionAlert: The first עָרוֹם means the ספר is bare (touched without a covering). It does not mean the person is undressed.

phrases.english: Because of the statement of Rabbi Parnakh —

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי פַּרְנָךְ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Parnakh said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
One who holds a Torah scroll bare,
is buried bare.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי פַּרְנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ברייתא's decree.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree discourages touching a bare ספר תורה, which רבי יוחנן condemns.

steps.title: Can 'buried bare' really be meant literally?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether he would really be buried without clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bare? Could that enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the plain meaning of 'buried bare'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being buried without clothing seems like a strange and unfitting punishment for this sin. So the words must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: could it enter your mind? (rejects a reading)

phrases.english: Bare — could that enter your mind?

steps.triggerLanguage: עָרוֹם סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal reading of רבי יוחנן's words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal meaning of נקבר ערום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A literal burial without clothes is an unreasonable punishment.

steps.title: רבי זירא: bare means without מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains 'bare' as being without מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי זירא said: bare, meaning without מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא reads 'bare' as a picture, not a literal statement. The person is 'bare' of מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the punishment is spiritual. The person arrives in the next world without his מצוות.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Zeira said:
Bare — without מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge with a figurative reading.

steps.title: Can he really lose all his מצוות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether he would really lose all his מצוות for this one act.
steps.simpleTranslation: Without מצוות? Could that enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's reading as too extreme.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing all of a lifetime's merit because of one wrong act seems far too harsh. So this reading also needs to be narrowed.

phrases.english: Without מצוות — could that enter your mind?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּלֹא מִצְוֹת סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's explanation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Losing all merit for one act is unreasonably harsh.

steps.title: Final reading: bare of that one מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'bare' means he loses only the מצוה he did while holding the bare ספר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: bare, meaning without that מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final meaning. The person loses credit only for the מצוה he did while touching the bare ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if he held the ספר to do a מצוה, such as reading or rolling it, he gets no credit for that מצוה, because he did it disrespectfully. This is a fair, limited punishment, and it explains why the רבנן discouraged touching a bare ספר.
steps.whatToRemember: Holding a bare ספר תורה makes you lose the מצוה you did with it. That is why the רבנן made hands that touch a ספר disqualify תרומה, to discourage touching it directly.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Bare — without that מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: עָרוֹם בְּלֹא אוֹתָהּ מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי זירא's reading to answer the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the statement
steps.terutzMaskana: He loses only the מצוה done while holding the bare ספר.

steps.title: Which decree about hands came first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the two hand-decrees the חכמים made first. It then starts testing one option: that the general decree on all hands (סתם ידים) came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which decree did they make first? If you say they made this one (the general decree on all hands) first,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which decree came first: the one about hands touching a ספר תורה, or the one about all hands. It then begins testing the first option. This step only sets things up, and the problem with that option comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate decrees that make hands impure for תרומה. One covers hands that touched a ספר. The other covers all hands, because hands are always busy touching things. The word אילימא tells us the גמרא is raising an option it plans to reject, since a general decree on all hands would seem to make the specific ספר decree unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: They decreed (the חכמים made a rabbinic decree)
If you say… (opens an option that will usually be rejected)
Hands in general: the decree that any hands are impure for תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop after reading אילימא and think this is the answer. אילימא almost always opens an option the גמרא is about to knock down. The real answer comes after the rejection.
steps.whyThisMatters: Figuring out the order shows that each decree had its own purpose. If the broad decree on all hands came first, a later decree about hands that touched a ספר would add nothing, because those hands were already included. If the narrow ספר decree came first, a later broader decree simply extends it, and both make sense.

phrases.english: Which did they decree first?
phrases.notes: Asks about the order of the two hand-decrees: hands touching a ספר, and hands in general.

phrases.english: If you say they decreed this one first,
phrases.notes: "This one" refers to the general decree on all hands (סתם ידים). The objection to this option comes next.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי גְּזוּר בְּרֵישָׁא? אִילֵימָא הָא גְּזוּר בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the explanation of the ספר תורה decree (steps 23-27), the גמרא now asks how it fits in time with the general decree on all hands.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which decree came first: hands touching a ספר, or hands in general (סתם ידים)?
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the general decree on all hands came first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all hands were already impure, a separate decree for hands touching a ספר would add nothing. This attack is set up here and stated in the next line.
